To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the binding of aluminum ions to the ligands containing a phenolic group(s)-8-hydroxy quinoline, salicyclic acid, N, N'-di(2 hydroxybenzyl)-ethylenediami-ne-N,N'-diacetate and N, N'-ethylenebis[ 2-(o-hy-droxyphenolic) glycine]-are different, and this is the key reason for the differences in the binding and releasing processes of ferric ions

the fluorescence of the ligands with the phenolic group(s)(salicylic acid, 8-HOQ, HBED, and EHPG) are different, which can be explained by the intramolecular hydrogen bonding between the phenolic hydroxyl and the other groups in the molecule.

aluminum binding to the ligand with phenolic group produces a UV difference band at 235 nm, the fluorescence emission of N,N'-di (2-hydroxy benzyl) ethy lenediamine-N, N'-diacetic acids and salicylic acid decreases, and the fluorescence emission of 8-hydroxylquinoline increases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the difference between the N- and C-termini in binding of ferric ions to the transferrin.
the difference between N- and the C-terminal binding sites in transferrin, which is due to the difference of the interactions between phenolic groups and the aluminum ion in these two sites.

the difference between N- and the C-terminal binding sites in human serum transferrins, and it has been demonstrated that the difference is due to the difference of the intramolecular hydrogen bonding of phenolic groups in these two binding sites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the differences in binding and releasing of aluminum between the C- and N-terminal binding site of transferrin are due to the different types of intramolecular hydrogen bonding in the phenolic groups.
the differences in binding and releasing of iron ions in the C-, and N-terminals of human serum transfertin are due to the differences in the intramolecular hydrogen bonding of phenolic group(s).
aluminum binds to the phenolic groups in both C- and N-terminal binding site of human serum transfertin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the differences between N cdots, centered and C-terminal binding of human serum transfirin for ferric ion are due to the difference between the O cdots, centered H-O and N cdots, center H-O type intrmolecular hydrogen bonds of the ligands in the two binding sites.
the N-terminal binding sites have a stronger affinity for ferric ions than do the C-terminal binding sites.

the N cdots, two dots, centered H-N type intramolecular H-bonding in the C-terminal site is stronger than in the N-terminal site and the O cdots, two, three dots, H-O type intrmolecular H-bond in the C-terminal is weaker than in the N terminal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the binding of aluminum to the phenolic groups in the C-terminal site of apotransferin is weaker than in the N-terminal site.
the difference between the N- and C- binding sites of human transferrin is the difference of the hydrogen bonding type between the phenolic groups and the protein.
the difference of aluminum ion binding to C- and N-terminal binding site of apotransserrin is due to the intramolecular hydrogen bonding of phenolic group(s).
